HCC serves over 9,000 students annually, and provides a variety of recreational and cultural activities, from sports programs to music festivals, for students and community members alike. The college's strongest assets continue to be an innovative spirit, a sincere concern for students and a commitment to strive for even greater success. Work with the department to build community, internship, and college transfer partnerships. Engage in enrollment, retention, and outreach activities in alignment with the department’s mission. Pursue grant opportunities and other sustainability projects Actively participates in department, division and professional staff meetings as well as other components of college governance.Participates in college programs and activities including holding office hours to support student success.The faculty members will be supportive of students' learning goals by: a.) jobs.title: Mitigation Specialist at State Appellate Defender Office
jobs.description: Employer: State Appellate Defender Office Expires: 10/15/2026 Join Michigan’s State Appellate Defender Office (SADO) as a full-time, limited-term Mitigation Specialist for the Private Counsel Division of SADO. The salary range for this position is $57,252 to $96,048, depending on experience. Mitigation specialists are supervised and trained by the Michigan Appellate Assigned Counsel System (MAACS) Administrator or the MAACS Roster Support and Performance Manager. This position can be based out of SADO’s Detroit or Lansing office. The position requires extensive travel (about 20% of the time) and offers a flexible hybrid work policy. Job ResponsibilitiesSpecific duties include, but are not limited to:Interview, and build rapport with incarcerated clients to learn about their background, the facts of the offense, current experiences while incarcerated, and specific needs upon release;Identify, locate, and interview family, friends, community members, and other individuals to compile material in mitigation of sentence;Travel extensively throughout Michigan and occasionally out of state to visit clients in prison and interview witnesses;Obtain, analyze, and summarize records and documents, including prison records, social files, school records, and medical and mental health records;Prepare reports, including client and witness interview memos, social history reports, and sentencing memoranda, using creative writing and storytelling techniques;Identify support for clients transitioning back into the community;Identify and consult with appropriate experts to obtain reports and prepare for hearings;Prepare clients for testifying in court or presenting allocution; In limited circumstances, testify in court;Train attorneys and staff on mitigation and parole hearings; andAssist attorneys with general hearing preparation such as preparing exhibits, coordinating with witnesses, attending court hearings, and other necessary tasks.QualificationsMitigation specialists draw from a diverse range of professional, academic, and life experiences to inform their work. Mitigation specialists must be empathetic communicators, effective interviewers, curious investigators, critical readers, data managers, creative writers, compassionate listeners, and zealous advocates. At SADO we are dedicated to building a multi-disciplinary team with diverse perspectives and experiences, so if you are excited about this role but you do not meet every qualification in this job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be the right candidate for the job.Education: Education and/or equivalent experience in social work, social sciences, psychology, forensic psychology, journalism, anthropology, criminal justice, or a related field;Commitments:Commitment to client-centered, zealous advocacy; Commitment to the inherent worth and dignity of clients;Commitment to cultural humility and cultural competency;Knowledge and Abilities:Knowledge of the criminal legal system, preferably in Michigan; Experience in investigation;Excellent communication, trauma-informed interviewing, and interpersonal skills;Understanding of mental health signs and symptoms, the effects of trauma, developmental and intellectual disabilities, and the impacts of social, cultural, historical, political, religious, racial, environmental, and ethnic influences on behavior;Ability to prioritize multiple client cases, deadlines, and demands;Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings, nights, and early mornings, and to travel throughout the state to attend hearings, meet with incarcerated clients, interview witnesses, and obtain mitigation material;Possess a valid driver’s license;Ability to organize, interpret, and synthesize large quantities of information into persuasive, compelling, and thorough written narratives;Flexible and creative thinking;The ability to work as part of the defense team under the lead of the case attorney, and maintain confidentiality;Proficiency with Microsoft Word and Outlook, Adobe Acrobat, Excel, and general office equipment;Self-motivated, with the ability to handle constructive feedback; andCandidates must be a current resident of or relocate to Michigan by hire date.To ApplySubmit a resume and a cover letter via email by October 11, 2026, to jobs@sado.org and include “MAACS Mitigation Specialist 2026-13” in the subject line. Applications without a resume and cover letter will not be considered. The cover letter should address the reasons underlying your interest in the work and explain your commitment to working with incarcerated people and people convicted of crimes.SADO is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. A felony conviction does not prohibit employment at SADO.

jobs.description: Employer: One On One Basketball Expires: 10/15/2026 My name is Frank Luca, President of One on One Basketball RI. If you are looking for a fun and rewarding part time job, with good pay please see the job description below.We are looking for individuals to be part of a team of enthusiastic, motivated instructors. After School Hoops is an After School Basketball and Sports Program dedicated to the fundamental development of young players. Instructors will be meeting once a week, per school, at an assigned elementary or middle school, during a 6-8 week period. Classes meet anytime between 2:30-5:15 pm for 1-2 hrs. Our school programs run Monday-Friday excluding school holidays and vacations. Each instructor, depending on his or her schedule and preference, could be asked to teach between two to four afternoons per week at their assigned schools. jobs.title: Auxiliary Programs Team Member at Georgetown Day School
jobs.description: Employer: Georgetown Day School Expires: 10/15/2026 About the SchoolGeorgetown Day School opened its doors in 1945 as the first integrated school in a segregated city. GDS was founded by seven changemaker families who envisioned a school committed not only to academic excellence and educational innovation but also to respect and care for others. Believing that diversity is a critical foundation for the most transformational learning, they established a school where all children would be welcomed, celebrated, and challenged to be their best selves.Today, the School’s philosophy and programs strongly reflect its roots. GDS fosters a community of belonging while lifting up every student’s unique gifts, building in each the capacity for compassion, leadership, and creating positive change. 1125 engaged and talented PK-12 students across three divisions love to learn and learn to change the world in GDS’s exciting urban campus with its outstanding facilities. Recognized as one the most dynamic educational institutions in our capital city and nation, GDS today is in a uniquely attractive position, with a deeply-felt and lived history, clear mission, and genuine openness to the possibilities that lie ahead. Georgetown Day School’s (GDS) Office of Auxiliary Programs seeks staff to become part of its department (extended day programs) for the 2026-2027 school year.GDS Auxiliary Programs Mission:While participating in GDS Auxiliary Programs, children will explore, learn, and create through hands-on and interpersonal inquiry, gaining an appreciation for themselves, others, and the world. GDS Auxiliary Programs Team Members teach new skills and provide tools that enable children to develop into great people who strive to learn, understand, try new things, and care for others. Position Description:GDS seeks to hire several School Year Auxiliary Programs Team Members to support ongoing school year programming. We seek individuals with experience working with elementary and middle school-aged children (ages 4–13) who are prepared to challenge students academically, physically, and artistically and to establish authentic relationships with the children in the extended-day program. The ability to provide rich, mission-aligned, and creative content, to develop authentic relationships, to work collaboratively with colleagues, and to place children’s interests and experiences at the heart of the classroom are essential components of the job. Location: On-campus at 4200 Davenport Street NW, Washington, DC, 20016Start Date: Immediate start (once cleared to work)Type of Opportunity: Part-timeFLSA Status: Non-exempt Compensation: $21.32 to 31.90/hour, depending on years of experience (compensation for students starts at minimum wage)Note: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.Potential Hours and Work Functions:Extended Day (M/T/W/H/F - 2:30 - 6:30 p.m.)Early Morning Grasshopper (M/T/W/H/F - 7:00 - 8:00 am)Break Camp (Various days throughout the school year - 8:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m.)Staff Childcare (Various days throughout the school year - 8:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m.)External Relations (Various evenings and weekends - various times)These team members may plan weekly special activities to pique our students’ interests in a variety of ways. Responsibilities: Supervise an activity with an assigned class for a particular age group. Supervise snacks and be aware of food allergies. Supervise off-campus activities Supervise outside vendors/groups during on-campus rentals. Supervise and facilitate free-choice activities and recess. Support enrichment classes If assigned, work at the extended day help desk and/or carline. Develop weekly lesson plans for free-choice classes, including submission of material requests, etc. Ensure that students are learning in creative, hands-on, interactive, and age-appropriate ways. Incorporate opportunities for students to collaborate, problem-solve, and create Other duties as assignedThis position reports to the Director of GDS 360 Extended Day.Qualifications:After School Program or Summer Camp work experience, or other equivalent professional experience working with children Bachelor’s degree in education and/or 90 Hour Child Care Certification preferred, but not required. Previous teaching experience Ability to think on one’s feet Ability to work collaboratively Must enjoy working with children and demonstrate sound judgment Patience and a sense of humorPreference will be given to staff who can work 5 days a week. Must be able to work at a minimum of 3 days per week. Americans with Disability SpecificationsPhysical Demands:The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel objects, tools or controls; reach with hands and arms; climb stairs; balance; stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl; talk, see or hear. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Work Environment:Work environment characteristics described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is exposed to weather conditions prevalent at the time. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. To Apply:Qualified candidates should submit a cover letter, resume, and list of three references using our online application system through ADP/Workforce Now: http://www.gds.org/Recruiting. To find out more about the school, candidates should visit our website at www.gds.org. As an inclusive school devoted to preparing our students to live, work, and lead in an increasingly globalized and multicultural society, GDS is particularly interested in professionals with demonstrated interest and experience in working in such a school setting and is driven by the core charge of working to enhance and bring joy to every student’s individual learning experience in equitable and meaningful ways.

jobs.description: Employer: Behavioral Initiatives Expires: 10/15/2026 Job Description:The Behavior therapist or RBT provides intensive behavioral intervention services to individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder and language delays. The RBT will work teaching language, communication, academic, and life skills to individuals with autism using the methods of Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA). Teaching will be conducted in centers, homes, schools, and in the community. Training will be provided as well as regular supervision by a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA). Experience with children with autism and/or developmental disabilities preferred Experience in Applied Behavior Analysis preferredCertification: Registered Behavior TechnicianAll applicants must pass a background check Pay/BenefitsPay Range based on performance ($20-$23/hr) starting with the potential to make $27/hr plus bonus.RBT Certification Training (If Needed)Paid SupervisionWork/Life Balance: Paid Time Off acquired for each year of service for the first three yearsBonus: Accumulate Paid Time Off or Cash BonusOngoing career development and training in the field of Applied Behavior AnalysisSupervision for individuals pursuing BCBA or BCaBAMileage ReimbursementWorker’s Comp and Liability Insurance

jobs.title: Literacy Leader at St Nicks Alliance
jobs.description: Employer: St Nicks Alliance Expires: 10/15/2026 Literacy Leader (Part-Time, After-School)St. Nicks Alliance | North Brooklyn | Fall 2026Pay: $20.85/hourHours: Approximately 20 hours per week during the school yearSchedule: Weekday afternoons, roughly 2:00–6:00pm, plus one morning per week for professional developmentLocation: North Brooklyn — Williamsburg, Greenpoint, Bushwick, and Bed-Stuy school sitesHelp kids fall in love with reading.St. Nicks Alliance is looking for Literacy Leaders to lead after-school literacy programming at our elementary and middle school sites across North Brooklyn.You don't need a teaching certificate. You need experience leading groups of kids, genuine interest in literacy and youth development, and the willingness to be coached. We provide the curriculum, weekly professional development, and one-on-one instructional coaching — your job is to bring it to life for students.This is a good fit if you're a college student or recent graduate in education, English, or psychology; a paraprofessional or teaching assistant looking for additional hours; a teaching artist; or someone considering a career in education who wants real classroom experience with real support behind it.About St. Nicks AllianceSt. Nicks Alliance is a North Brooklyn community organization working to transform the lives of low- and moderate-income people through employment, education, housing, elder care, and social services. Our after-school programs serve children across North Brooklyn with literacy, arts, homework help, and social-emotional learning.What you'll doInstruction. Lead twice-weekly literacy lessons for groups of 10–20 elementary or middle school students using our internally developed curriculum. Provide targeted small-group and individual instruction incorporating Science of Reading elements and the day school's literacy techniques. Build lessons that draw on students' home culture, values, interests, and language.Assessment. Assess student work formally and informally to determine growth and next steps. Document learning through notes, work collection, and photos. Collect literacy outcome and attitudinal data for our School Success Model research program. Keep site directors and group leaders informed about each student's strengths and challenges.Professional development and coaching. Participate in mandatory weekly professional development and in regular coaching sessions with our Instructional Coach or Associate Director of Education. Give feedback to our curriculum writers on what's working and what isn't — Literacy Leaders genuinely shape the curriculum here.Collaboration. Work with the school's literacy team to align our curriculum with school goals. Coordinate with the BK Story Voyager coordinator on book selection and programming. Partner with reading specialists, tutors, teaching artists, and the school's SEL transformational coach.Safety and supervision. Follow DOHMH, OCFS, and CDC safety protocols. Stay actively engaged in supervising students across all program components — meals, transitions, outdoor play, field trips, arrival, and dismissal.What we're looking forAt least two years leading lessons or structured activities for groups of ten or more childrenCompetency in lesson leadership — effective transitions, student engagement, clear directionsAbility to build productive relationships with students while maintaining appropriate adult-child boundariesStrong self-awareness and interest in or experience with Social Emotional LearningPrior professional development in literacy, youth development, or teachingExceptional communication skills for working with leadership, program directors, colleagues, students, parents, and school facultyUnderstanding of the strengths and challenges of our students, including familiarity with their neighborhoods, cultures, languages, and valuesCapacity to adapt in dynamic after-school environmentsHelpful but not required: experience teaching project- or theme-based lessons; experience writing lesson plans with learning objectives; interest in advancing professionally in education, literacy, or child development.Why this job is worth havingMost part-time youth jobs hand you a room and wish you luck. This one comes with a written curriculum, weekly paid professional development, and an instructional coach whose job is helping you get better. People who want to teach use this role to find out whether they actually do — and to build the skills before they commit to a credential program.How to applySend a resume and a cover letter explaining why you are the right person for this role at St. Nicks Alliance to Tim Fredrick at tfredrick@stnicksalliance.org, with "Literacy Leader" in the subject line. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.St. Nicks Alliance is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to building a staff that reflects the communities we serve, and we encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds.

jobs.description: Employer: Holyoke Community College - Human Resources Expires: 10/15/2026 About Holyoke Community College:Holyoke Community College is housed on a multi-million-dollar, 135-acre campus, equipped with state-of-the art technology in specialized learning facilities. HCC serves over 9,000 students annually, and provides a variety of recreational and cultural activities, from sports programs to music festivals, for students and community members alike. The college's strongest assets continue to be an innovative spirit, a sincere concern for students and a commitment to strive for even greater success. These are the values which have created a tradition of excellence spanning more than six decades, and which are enabling Holyoke Community College to meet today's challenges.Mission: Educate. Inspire. Connect.Values: Kindness, Inclusion, Trust, Innovation & CollaborationKindness, inclusion and trust are the foundation of the work that we do together. Innovation and collaboration enable us to explore and implement the ideas that will shape our future. At HCC’s Business Department, we’re more than just a learning community—we’re a dynamic team where innovation, collaboration, and progress thrive. Our goal is to inspire the next generation of business leaders through hands-on, practical education that connects classroom learning to real-world success.We offer diverse certificate, career, and transfer programs that help students strengthen communication, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills while building meaningful professional and community connections. We celebrate diversity and inclusion, seeking educators who bring fresh ideas and value collaboration in shaping a welcoming, forward-thinking environment.For this Accounting Faculty position, we’re looking for an educator who is passionate about teaching - whether on-site, online, or in a hybrid format - and who brings real-world accounting experience to life for students. The ideal candidate communicates complex concepts clearly, embraces innovation and technology, and contributes to the department’s supportive culture. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds, particularly those from historically underrepresented groups, to join us in creating an inclusive and inspiring place to learn and grow. Develop innovative methods for teaching accounting and business-related courses such as Principles of Accounting, Managerial Accounting, Computerized Accounting and Principles of Business. Expected to teach in all and any combination of modalities - On Site, Online and Hybrid, with emphasis on site.The faculty member will utilize active learning methods and use a variety of instructional strategies designed to assist the learner in meeting the objectives of the course in a variety of modalities. Such activities can include, but are not limited to: Cooperative - project based learning Experiential learning - community based learning, learning community Technology-enhanced learning Critical thinking initiatives.Participate in curriculum development and continuous improvement to meet current industry standards and credential requirements. They will remain abreast of ongoing developments and practices in their professional content area(s).Integrate computer technology and relevant accounting software (e.g., QuickBooks, Excel, data analytics tools and artificial intelligence) into coursework, as appropriate.Provide student advising on academic, career, and transfer opportunities aligned with Business Department pathways. Collaborate with colleagues within the department, across divisions, and through College Governance Committees and task forces. Contribute to program assessment, general education outcomes assessment and student learning outcomes initiatives. Work with the department to build community, internship, and university transfer partnerships. Engage in enrollment, retention, and outreach activities in alignment with the department’s mission. Pursue grant opportunities and other sustainability projects Actively participates in department, division and professional staff meetings as well as other components of college governance.Participates in college programs and activities including holding office hours to support student success.The faculty members will be supportive of students' learning goals by: a.) Focusing on student learning outcomes b.) Taking into account the needs and abilities of the students c.) Becoming familiar with academic and social support while making reasonable provisions to accommodate individual differences.Maintain academic integrity, foster inclusive learning environments, and promote HCC’s mission and values. Minimum Qualifications: Master’s degree in Accounting, Business, or a closely related field. Certified Public Accountant or other relevant professional certification.Experience designing and teaching engaging courses, including online, hybrid, or in-person formats.Demonstrated ability to apply inclusive, student-centered teaching practices and varied pedagogical strategies. Ability to integrate technology into instruction, including QuickBooks and other accounting and business applications. Willingness to teach across multiple modalities (on-campus, hybrid, and online). Excellent written and oral communication skills. Commitment to the mission of the community college. Demonstrated success teaching and mentoring a diverse student population. Equivalency Statement:We welcome and encourage applicants who do not meet the qualifications as stated above, to put in writing precisely how their background and experience have prepared them for the responsibilities of this position. It is preferred that this document be uploaded separately from the resume, cover letter, and references. Preferred Qualifications:Post-Master’s credits or doctoral degree in Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.Certified Public Accountant or other relevant professional certification. Demonstrated proficiency in community college teaching and online course delivery. Experience teaching introductory and advanced accounting courses. Experience using advanced accounting software and data analytics tools. Ability to contribute to interdisciplinary instruction within the Business Department. Experience fostering partnerships with community organizations or local businesses. Full-Time, Tenure-Track MCCC/MTA Position:Salary Range: $58,722.00 - $77,865.00. Actual salary will be commensurate with education and experience in accordance with MCCC/MTA Collective Bargaining Agreement. Full State benefits. Funding: State.Start Date: January, 2027.Additional Details:A teaching demonstration is a required part of the interview process.Applications received by October 2, 2026, will receive priority consideration. The position will remain open until filled.In addition to the application, submission of the following documents is required:Letter of interest (Cover Letter). When preparing the cover letter, please refer to the minimum and preferred qualifications. CV/Resume including three references with contact information (email and phone). Disability Accommodations:Holyoke Community College is committed to the full inclusion of individuals with disabilities and will ensure the availability of reasonable accommodations. If a reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, please contact the Office of People and Talent at (413) 552-2554.Background Check:Employment is contingent upon the successful completion and review of a background check which will include CORI (Criminal Offender Record Information) and SORI (Sex Offender Registry Information).All candidates must have legal authorization to work in the United States. HCC is not sponsoring H1B Visa. Holyoke Community College is an affirmative action/equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, disability, religion, age, veteran status, genetic information, gender identity or sexual orientation in its programs and activities as required by Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, and other applicable statutes and college policies. The College prohibits sexual harassment, including sexual violence. Inquiries or complaints concerning discrimination, harassment, retaliation or sexual violence shall be referred to the College’s Affirmative Action and/or Title IX Coordinator, the Massachusetts Commission Against Discrimination, the Equal Employment Opportunities Commission or the United States Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights.

jobs.description: Employer: LearnWell Expires: 10/15/2026 At LearnWell, we are committed to changing the lives of the 10 million students in the U.S. who are dealing with behavioral health issues. For more than 26 years, we have provided on-site educational services in hospitals, helping these school-age patients continue their education during treatment and reintegrate successfully into the classroom. jobs.description: Employer: Grand Rapids Community College Expires: 10/15/2026 Associate Dean of the School of Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM)Department: STEMLocation: Grand Rapids, MISUMMARYThe Associate Dean supports the School of STEM through innovative, student-focused leadership, fostering a collaborative environment that prioritizes academic excellence, inclusion, and community impact at GRCC. The Associate Dean works in cooperation with Department Heads and Program Directors to develop class schedules, determine instructional workloads, and support the implementation of the curriculum development process. The Associate Dean also provides leadership and oversight of faculty professional development, evaluations, and tenure and promotion activities. Program/Curriculum Review and Support - In collaboration with Department Heads and Program Directors, implement approved new/revised courses and programs.- Support the Dean in disseminating and utilizing data relevant to School departments/programs concerning student success, retention, completion, post-completion, transfer, or other trends.- Assist the Dean in identifying fundraising and grant development opportunities related to academic departments/programs, including Perkins (if applicable).- Collaborate with and support the Dean on curricular processes and decision-making.- Collaborate with and support ASA leaders (Provost direct reports, Associate Provosts' Offices, Associate Dean colleagues, Registrar's Office, Institutional Research, and Teaching, Learning, and Distance Education (TLDE) staff/faculty) on college-wide curricular processes and decision-making.- Represent the School on college-wide curriculum and/or learning outcomes assessment teams, as appropriate and in collaboration with the Dean to ensure School representation.- Collaborate with ASA leaders for non-credit to credit curriculum alignment, as appropriate. Faculty Administration and Support - Collaborate with Dean and Program Directors and Department Heads to support and provide a comprehensive onboarding experience and continuous reinforcement of departmental goals for department leaders and faculty.- Support Department Heads and Program Directors during program development and evaluation processes.- Approve Faculty Leaves of Absence and Substitute Instructor Compensation, and provide support documentation to Dean for budget-related processes associated with these operations.- Administer contract provisions for faculty and direct staff reports.- Approve adjunct professional development funds.- Monitor the textbook adoption process to ensure resources are accessible and available for classroom instruction through alignment with bookstore timelines.- Serve as the point of contact to address day-to-day faculty operations issues within the School. Faculty Evaluation - Supervise full-time and adjunct faculty in their respective areas.- Lead and administer the Faculty Evaluation System for the School, including annual Faculty Performance Evaluations (FPEs) and the tenure and promotion process. This includes collaborating with colleagues to provide orientation and training for faculty and working with other college leaders to ensure the effective operation of the system and related processes and supporting materials.- In collaboration with the Department Heads and Program Directors, form and facilitate tenure and promotion committees, and make tenure and promotion recommendations to the Dean.- Conduct faculty classroom observations and provide constructive written and verbal feedback as part of the evaluation process.- In collaboration with the Dean and Human Resources, as appropriate, create Performance Improvement Plans (PIP) for faculty and staff and take disciplinary action when needed. jobs.title: Lead Teacher, Early Childhood at Big Dreams Child Care
jobs.description: Employer: Big Dreams Child Care Expires: 10/15/2026 OverviewBig Dreams Child Care is a licensed early childhood education center serving families in southern Brooklyn from our Avenue U location. Our program spans infants through Pre-K, and we are building a teaching team defined by professionalism, consistency, and high expectations for both children and adults.We are hiring Lead Teachers who are able to effectively lead a classroom and be held to a professional standard. The role carries real responsibility: you set the tone for your room, lead the assistant teachers assigned to it, and serve as a point contact for the families in your care. In return, you will work within a transparent environment, receive direct support from our Educational Director focused on classroom quality, and have a defined path for advancement within the organization.This position is based exclusively at our Avenue U center.Job DescriptionThe Lead Teacher is responsible for the safety, development, and daily experience of every child in the assigned classroom; the quality and consistency of the educational program; full compliance with NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene Article 47 regulations; the relationship with each enrolled family; and the direction and performance of the Assistant Teachers assigned to the room. This is a non-exempt, full-time position reporting to the Educational Director.ResponsibilitiesClassroom leadership and instructionPlan and deliver a developmentally appropriate daily program for the assigned age group, aligned to the center's curriculum framework, with structured routines, small-group instruction, and purposeful playEstablish and maintain classroom routines, transitions, and behavior expectations that create a calm, predictable environment for childrenDifferentiate instruction and care to meet the individual needs of each child, including children with developmental or behavioral support needsHealth, safety, and complianceMaintain required staff-to-child ratios at all times and manage coverage transitions with the Educational DirectorComplete daily attendance, health checks, incident reports, and all required documentation accurately and on the same dayKeep the classroom inspection-ready under Article 47 standards, including health, hygiene, allergy, and safe-sleep protocols where applicableServe as a mandated reporter and follow all center policies regarding child protectionAssessment and family engagementConduct ongoing developmental observations and complete periodic assessments for each child as directedCommunicate with families daily through Brightwheel and in person at drop-off and pick-upRespond to family questions and concerns the same day, and escalate to the Educational Director when appropriateRepresent the center professionally in every family interactionTeam leadershipDirect the daily work of one to three Assistant Teachers: assign responsibilities, model expectations, and provide real-time feedbackContribute to the performance evaluations of assigned Assistant TeachersEnsure the classroom operates to standard during your planning time, breaks, and absences by preparing your team accordinglyProfessional conductMaintain reliable, punctual attendance in accordance with the center's attendance and call-out policy. Children and colleagues depend on your presence, and this expectation is fundamental to the role.Participate in staff meetings, required training hours, and scheduled performance reviewsAdhere to the employee handbook and all center policiesQualificationsRequiredNYC Article 47 group teacher qualified: NYS Early Childhood (Birth to Grade 2) certification, or a bachelor's or associate degree in early childhood education or a related field with an approved study plan toward certificationMinimum of one year of experience as the lead teacher of a classroom in a licensed early childhood programAbility to obtain and maintain all NYC DOHMH clearances, including fingerprinting, Statewide Central Register (SCR) clearance, medical clearance and immunizations, CPR and First Aid certification, and mandated reporter trainingStrong written and verbal communication skills in EnglishProficiency with classroom management technology (Brightwheel or comparable platform)Physical ability to lift up to 40 pounds, sit on the floor, stand for extended periods, and respond quickly to children's needsPreferredTwo or more years of lead classroom experienceNYS Early Childhood certification or a master's degree in early childhood educationExperience with infant or toddler classroomsBilingual proficiency (Russian, Spanish, Mandarin, or Hebrew)Performance standards. Lead Teachers are evaluated each September and January. Results determine placement within the pay scale and eligibility for advancement. New hires complete a 90-day introductory period with structured check-ins at 30, 60, and 90 days.Our standard. We hold Lead Teachers to the highest standard of professionalism in early childhood education, and we are deliberate about who we hire. A Lead Teacher at Big Dreams is a model of our mission and vision, in and out of the classroom: in how you prepare, how you speak to children, how you lead your team, how you present yourself to families, and how reliably you show up. Families entrust us with their children on the strength of the people we put in front of them, and every Lead Teacher is expected to be worthy of that trust every day. We look for teachers who take ownership without being asked, hold themselves accountable before anyone else has to, treat the standard as a source of pride rather than a burden, and raise the level of the people around them. If that describes how you work, you will find a center that backs you, invests in you, and rewards you for it.Big Dreams Child Care is an equal opportunity employer. All employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

The coordinator is responsible for the administration, monitoring, and reporting of program activities, including eligibility determination, meal counts, and reimbursement claims. other federally funded child nutrition programs.Strong working knowledge of United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) regulations and guidelines governing school nutrition programs.Proficiency in data management systems and reporting software used for program administration and compliance.Excellent organizational, time management, and written and verbal communication skills.PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:ServSafe Certification required and must be renewed every five (5) yearsExperience in training and supervising food service personnel.Familiarity with state-specific NSLP policies and procedures.Advanced skills in spreadsheet and database management.KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:Manage daily operations of the National School Lunch Program, ensuring adherence to USDA guidelines and regulations.Conduct eligibility determinations for free and reduced-price meal applications and maintain accurate records.Prepare and submit timely reimbursement claims and required reports the Business OfficeTrain and support Food Service Management Company (FSMC) on program requirements, meal pattern standards, and recordkeeping.Review monthly meal count from FSMC for accuracy and forward the report to Pennsylvania Department of Education (PDE) for processing through the PEARS or other approved systemMonitor program compliance through regular audits and reviews, implementing corrective actions as needed.Collaborate with school administrators, parents, and community organizations to promote program participation and nutrition education.Maintain up-to-date knowledge of policy changes and provide guidance to ensure ongoing compliance.Consults with Operations Manager regarding purchasing and required requests for proposals (RFP)/Requests for Quotes (RFQ)Develop and implement strategies to improve meal quality, participation rates, and operational efficiency.Perform other duties as requested by the Operations Manager, or Administrator in accordance with school policies and practicesSKILLS:The NSLP Program Coordinator utilizes their knowledge of federal nutrition program regulations daily to ensure all meal services comply with legal standards, which requires attention to detail and regulatory understanding. Analytical skills are used to review program data, identify trends, and implement improvements to increase efficiency and meal quality. Additionally, proficiency with data management tools supports accurate reporting and compliance monitoring, enabling the coordinator to maintain program integrity and secure funding.

jobs.description: Employer: Leila Day Nurseries Expires: 10/15/2026 Employment DetailsPosition: Preschool Afternoon Teacher AssistantType: Part-Time, Non-exemptCompensation: $18-$21/hour, based on education and experienceSchedule: Monday–Friday, 2:00–5:30 PM (17.5 hours/week)Location: New Haven, CT (On-site)Additional Work Opportunities: Additional paid work for substitute shifts may be available based on school needs and employee interest.Occasional Required Activities: Staff may occasionally be asked to participate in professional development or school events outside of their regular schedule; any required hours outside the regular schedule will be paid. About Leila DayLeila Day is a progressive, play-based, nature-centered school where childhood is honored. We innovate and build on the best traditions and practices of progressive, early childhood education. We believe in teaching and learning grounded in caring relationships, filled with joyful, learning adventures, and powered by the creativity of children at play. Teachers plan learning experiences around the needs and interests of the children and the opportunities provided by the natural world and our multicultural community. Our indoor and outdoor classrooms encourage children to explore, wonder, learn, and grow. Located beside East Rock Park in New Haven, we use the woods, trails, streams, and surrounding neighborhood as an extension of the classroom. Position SummaryThe Afternoon Assistant Teacher supports the preschool teaching team in creating an engaging, developmentally appropriate learning environment rooted in children's interests, meaningful relationships, and joyful exploration. Working alongside lead teachers, this role helps implement an emergent curriculum that encourages curiosity, creativity, experimentation, and play. The Assistant Teacher contributes to a classroom culture that reflects Leila Day's commitment to progressive early childhood education, emphasizing inquiry, emotional intelligence, outdoor learning, collaboration, and respect for every child. Key ResponsibilitiesSupport lead teachers in implementing classroom activities, learning experiences, and an emergent curriculum responsive to children's interests and needs.Engage actively with children during play, exploration, routines, and transitions, helping create a welcoming, joyful, and developmentally appropriate classroom environment.Support children's social-emotional development by encouraging positive self-concept, respectful relationships, and an appreciation for each child's cultural background, language, interests, and individual learning style.Help prepare and maintain indoor and outdoor learning environments, including setting up materials, organizing supplies, and caring for classroom equipment and shared spaces.Support daily classroom routines and group management under the direction of lead or co-teachers, including transitions, limit-setting, behavioral expectations, and other practices that promote children's safety and well-being.Communicate and collaborate effectively with lead teachers, co-teachers, families, and colleagues to support children's experiences and the work of the teaching team.Participate in ongoing professional learning and engage with current research and best practices in early childhood education.Contribute to the broader Leila Day community through collaboration with colleagues and participation in relevant staff meetings, professional development, and school activities. Required QualificationsMust be at least 18 years of age.Minimum 1-2 years of childcare, classroom, camp, babysitting, or youth development experience. Physical, Health & Safety RequirementsAbility to meet applicable Connecticut licensing requirements and Leila Day health and safety requirements, including required health documentation and training such as CPR, First Aid, and Administration of Medication, as applicable to the position.Ability to safely supervise and respond to children in a variety of indoor and outdoor environments.Ability to participate in the physical activities of the position, including walking, running, climbing, squatting, kneeling, sitting on the floor, and lifting, moving, or assisting children.Ability and willingness to spend significant portions of the school day outdoors in a variety of weather conditions.Ability to respond appropriately and promptly to children's health and safety needs and to emergency or unexpected situations. Preferred QualificationsEarly Childhood Education (ECE) coursework or creditsExperience teaching or learning in an outdoor education settingProfessional Growth & Additional OpportunitiesOngoing professional development opportunitiesOpportunities to work substitute shifts based on school needs and employee interestOpportunities for career growth within Leila DayDaily opportunities to learn and work alongside children in Leila Day's outdoor classrooms and surrounding natural environment.Part-time, hourly employees will be paid for holidays or weather-related closings that fall during their regular work schedule. Pay will be based on the employees’ normal hours scheduled on the day the event occurs. Holidays that occur during recess weeks will not be doubly compensated.How to ApplyPlease click Apply Now [LINK] to submit your resume and cover letter through our online application system. We review applications on a rolling basis and encourage interested candidates to apply early. If you experience technical difficulties with the application, please contact us at office@leiladay.org.Our Commitment to InclusionAt Leila Day Nursery School, we believe children thrive in communities rooted in belonging, curiosity, dignity, and care. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace that reflects the families and communities we serve. We welcome candidates of all backgrounds and lived experiences and encourage anyone who shares our commitment to joyful, equitable, child-centered education to apply.

As an RBT at Lighthouse, you can expect to:Deliver One-on-One ABA Therapy: Work with children ranging from 18 months to school age, using your expertise to provide personalized therapy.Collaborate with a Multidisciplinary Team: Develop and implement customized therapy plans with the support of our skilled team.Apply Creativity in Therapy: Use advanced techniques in our play-based and naturalistic therapy environment.Guide Children's Progress: Help children succeed in educational and social settings, preparing them for successful transitions.Document and Track Development: Contribute to each child's therapy program by meticulously documenting their progress.Embody Core Values: Thrive in a supportive team environment that upholds our values of Compassion, Trustworthiness, Courage, and Commitment.Join us in becoming a Lighthouse Legend and shaping a brighter future for children with autism. Apply now and let's make a difference together! RequirementsAssociate or Bachelor's degree highly preferred.Lifting/Carrying more than 50 lbs. Able to sustain impact to body (i.e., being hit, etc.) in any area. Running, crouching, squatting, and ability to kneel for sustained periods of time. Bending at the waist to touch knees and/or toes. jobs.description: Employer: League School of Greater Boston Expires: 10/15/2026 At League School for Autism, our mission is to open a world of opportunity for student growth by celebrating unique strengths and building an inclusive community through education and advocacy. We believe that behind every thriving student is a team of remarkable, dedicated Educators, Clinicians, and support staff.We are currently seeking a TEACHER ASSISTANT for our year-round program in Walpole, MA. Starting pay rate is $22.50 - $26.40/hour, depending on years of experience and level of education completed. Schedule: M-F 7:00 a.m. – 3:00 p.m. Position Requirements:Associate's Degree or specialized training in a related field or experience working with autistic individuals strongly preferredPara-professional, Teacher’s Aide, or other special education experience preferredSafety Care, CPR, and First Aid certifications (League School will provide training)Valid driver’s licenseMust pass rigorous background checks, including nationwide fingerprint screening. Duties and Responsibilities include the following:Implements lessons and tasks, according to Individual Education Programs, within the classroom/school and community settings.Supervises students at community-based job sites and provides job-coaching services for students according to individual program needs. Transports students in League School vans as needed.Acts as liaison for communication between community-based employers and League School for Autism’s Vocational Coordinator according to individual program needs.Participates in the development of curriculum content, behavior intervention strategies and daily living-skill techniques for individual students and follows through on the strategies developed by the team.Collects and records data regarding student performance in instructional and behavioral areas.Develops a therapeutic and effective relationship with students: uses appropriate voice modulation, sets reasonable boundaries with communication and actions, etc.Follows schedules within the classroom and the school to provide structure and limit stimuli for the students.Implements student behavior programs: positive reinforcement breaks, time outs, etc., as designed by the Behavior Department and the team.Completes daily paperwork, as needed, to include: notes to parents, Incident Reports, Accident Reports, etc.Monitors health and safety of students and follows through with the School Nurse on incidents requiring medical attention.Works as a team player. Attends supervision, classroom meetings, program meetings and staff meetings. Comes prepared with agenda and ready to discuss issues and solutions.Participates in all trainings, as required by League School for Autism.Performs other related duties, as assigned by the Education Coordinator, Assistant Director of Education or Director of Education, that are deemed necessary for the operation of the school, such as evening trainings, Open House, etc. Physical Demands:The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. The employee must lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is required to stand, walk, run, sit, use hands, reach with hands and arms, climb or balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.Employees are required to intervene with student behavior according to the guidelines of Safety Care. These interventions may involve blocking aggressions and restraining students. These physical management procedures may require the employee to move from standing to kneeling, kneeling to standing, and to use both of their arms to restrict movement. Computer Skills:To perform this job successfully, an individual should have knowledge of Microsoft Office and Google Suite. Benefits:We provide a Total Well-being Package designed to protect your physical and mental health, secure your financial future, and support your overall well-being:77% Employer-Paid Health & Dental Insurance $100 Monthly Wellness Allowance (tailored to your choice) Financial Well-Being & Security: 403(b) retirement plan with employer match, short/long-term disability, and life insurance Growth & Tuition Assistance: Up to $5,000 per school year plus ongoing professional development Generous Paid Time Off: School vacation weeks, sick, and personal days to support work-life harmony Equal Opportunity EmployerLeague School for Autism is committed to maintaining a work and learning environment that is free from discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, pregnancy, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, ancestry, place of birth, age, citizenship status, veteran status, political affiliation, genetic information or disability, as defined and required by federal and state laws. Additionally, we prohibit retaliation against individuals who challenge such discrimination and harassment or who participate in an equal opportunity investigation. jobs.title: Sign Language Staff Interpreter at VersAbility Resources
jobs.description: Employer: VersAbility Resources Expires: 10/15/2026 About VersAbility ResourcesVersAbility Resources is a nonprofit organization based in Hampton, Virginia, dedicated to empowering people of all abilities to thrive. For more than 70 years, we have provided innovative employment, workforce development, residential, community living, and business services that promote independence, inclusion, and opportunity.Our team is passionate about making a meaningful impact by helping individuals achieve their personal and professional goals while delivering high-quality services to our community, business partners, and government customers. At VersAbility, you'll join a mission-driven organization where your work changes lives and contributes to stronger, more inclusive communities.Role OverviewThis is more than a new position—it is an important investment in communication access and inclusion at VersAbility Resources. VersAbility Resources is excited to welcome our first Sign Language Staff Interpreter, a permanent role dedicated to strengthening communication access for our Deaf and hard-of-hearing employees across the organization.Rather than relying solely on interpreting support for individual meetings or events, this position creates consistent, ongoing access to a professional who understands our employees, our workplaces, and the environments in which our teams work. For our Deaf and hard-of-hearing employees, that means greater continuity and access during orientations, training, meetings, workplace conversations, and other important moments throughout their employment experience.The Sign Language Staff Interpreter will provide professional American Sign Language (ASL)/English interpreting services across VersAbility locations, including Government Contract sites throughout Hampton Roads, while also providing virtual support to employees at geographically dispersed locations such as San Diego and Hawaii. This individual will help facilitate accurate, effective, and culturally responsive communication while respecting each employee's autonomy, communication preferences, confidentiality, and individual needs.If you are an experienced interpreter who believes communication access is essential to an inclusive workplace and wants the opportunity to become a trusted, consistent part of an organization rather than moving from assignment to assignment, this is an opportunity to make a lasting impact.What You'll DoProvide accurate, real-time, two-way interpretation between spoken English and ASL.Interpret workplace conversations, meetings, orientations, training, administrative discussions, healthcare-related interactions, technical information, and other organizational communications.Convey the complete meaning, intent, tone, context, and emotional nuance of communication rather than relying on word-for-word interpretation.Adapt interpreting approaches based on individual communication preferences, language proficiency, cultural considerations, and assignment needs.Provide interpreting support for regularly scheduled New Employee Orientation (NEO) and other organizational meetings, training, and events.Travel to VersAbility locations and Government Contract sites throughout Hampton Roads to provide on-site interpreting support.Provide virtual interpreting services for geographically dispersed VersAbility locations, including locations such as Hawaii and San Diego.Prepare for assignments by reviewing materials and becoming familiar with relevant terminology, acronyms, technical information, and subject matter.Collaborate with Deaf interpreters and other hearing interpreters during team-interpreting assignments.Coordinate appropriately with employees, managers, Human Resources, Supported Employment staff, and other stakeholders to support successful interpreting assignments.Maintain confidentiality, impartiality, professional boundaries, and ethical standards consistent with applicable professional interpreting standards, including the RID Code of Professional Conduct.Maintain required schedules, records, certifications, credentials, security clearances, and professional qualifications.Participate in continuing education, professional development, meetings, and required training.Perform other related duties as assigned.Qualifications RequiredHigh school diploma or GED equivalent.Minimum of one (1) year of professional ASL/English interpreting experience.Virginia Quality Assurance Screening (VQAS) Level III or above.Advanced proficiency in American Sign Language and spoken English.Strong understanding of Deaf culture, hearing culture, cultural norms, communication preferences, and culturally responsive interpreting practices.Knowledge of professional interpreting ethics, confidentiality, impartiality, professional boundaries, and the RID Code of Professional Conduct.Valid state-issued driver's license with an acceptable driving record.Ability and willingness to travel regularly between VersAbility locations and assigned Government Contract sites throughout Hampton Roads.REAL ID-compliant identification or valid U.S. Passport, or ability to obtain the required identification before the start date, for applicable military installation access.Ability to obtain and maintain required military installation/base access credentials and authorizations.Ability to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance when required for an assigned Government Contract location.Ability to use Microsoft Office, Outlook, Teams, virtual meeting platforms, cameras, headsets, and other technology necessary for remote interpreting.PreferredBachelor's degree in American Sign Language/English Interpretation, Interpreter Education, ASL Studies, or a related field.Two to three years of professional interpreting experience.National Interpreter Certification (NIC).Experience interpreting in employment, government, healthcare, educational, technical, or other professional environments.ScheduleThis is a full-time, permanent position working 40 hours per week.Monday–Friday | 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.Because interpreting needs occur across different VersAbility programs, locations, and time zones, candidates must be flexible to adjust their schedule based on employee communication needs, interpreting assignments, orientations, meetings, training, organizational events, and operational requirements. Regular local travel throughout Hampton Roads is required. The position will also provide virtual interpreting support for geographically dispersed VersAbility locations, including locations such as San Diego and Hawaii.Work Environment & Physical RequirementsThis is a dynamic interpreting position rather than a role based in one work environment. Assignments may take place in professional offices, orientation and training environments, VersAbility facilities, community locations, Government Contract sites, military installations, and virtual environments.Depending on the assignment, work environments may include changing lighting, varying temperatures, moderate to loud noise, distractions, outdoor conditions, or industrial and operational settings. Some assignments may involve lengthy, complex, technical, sensitive, or emotionally demanding communication.The position requires sustained concentration and visual attention, continuous and repetitive use of the hands, fingers, wrists, arms, and shoulders for ASL, and the upper-body stamina necessary for extended interpreting assignments. Regular travel between work locations and frequent entry and exit from a vehicle are also required.Candidates must be able to perform the essential duties and physical requirements of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation. VersAbility Resources provides reasonable accommodations in accordance with applicable law.Why Join Us?Help build something new. You will step into a newly created permanent role and help strengthen how VersAbility provides consistent communication access across the organization.Make an impact employees can experience every day. Your work will help Deaf and hard-of-hearing employees more fully access workplace communication, training, meetings, resources, and opportunities.Build continuity and trust. As a staff interpreter, you will have the opportunity to become familiar with our employees, terminology, teams, and work environments—supporting more consistent communication over time.Experience variety in your work. Assignments may take you from orientations and employee meetings to Government Contract environments, training sessions, virtual meetings, and other workplace settings.Use your profession to advance inclusion. Your expertise will directly support VersAbility's commitment to creating workplaces where employees of all abilities have meaningful access and opportunities to thrive.Grow with the role. As a new position within VersAbility, you will have the opportunity to help establish strong practices and contribute your professional perspective as our interpreting needs evolve.How to ApplyApply online through VersAbility Resources' careers site. If you need assistance or reasonable accommodation during the application process, please contact us at wehire@versability.org.Equal Opportunity EmployerVersAbility Resources is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to providing fair and equitable employment opportunities. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We value diversity and encourage applicants of all backgrounds to apply. Certain positions are performed under the federal AbilityOne Program and are subject to applicable contractual and program requirements.VersAbility Resources is committed to a drug-free workplace in line with the Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1988, ensuring a safe, productive environment. It also promotes equal opportunity for all, offering reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities to perform job duties. For assistance with applications, people can contact 757-896-6461.

jobs.title: Affective Needs Teacher at KIPP Colorado
jobs.description: Employer: KIPP Colorado Expires: 10/15/2026 This role comes with a $5,000 signing bonus*About the KIPP Colorado Special Education Teacher Role: The Special Education Teacher is the instructional leader of their student caseload and is directly responsible for driving student outcomes and creating an exceptional student experience. Teachers drive the educational mission of KIPP Colorado schools by developing daily instruction aligned with our academic program that enables students to make significant academic growth each year. The Special Education Teacher plans instruction, organizes learning activities, internalizes and intellectually prepares for lessons, grades equitably and consistently, and implements with fidelity all accommodations and modifications for students’ IEPs, BIP’s, 504 Plans, and MTSS interventions. The Special Education Teacher at KIPP Colorado holds full responsibility for creating and cultivating a culturally responsive classroom community that is warm-demanding, including upholding school-wide expectations, managing tier 1 behaviors, and contacting families proactively and responsively. Special Education Teacher Teachers support the campus-wide community and whole school systems through active presence at daily duties, including but not limited to: arrival duty, dismissal duty, lunch duty, threshold presence at transitions, hallway / bathroom duty, and coverage for staff absences. The position is a 10-month academic position and is exempt under the Fair Labor Standards Act. This position reports to a member of the school leadership team. About KIPP: Together with families and communities, KIPP creates joyful, academically excellent schools that prepare students with the skills and confidence to pursue the paths they choose—college, career, and beyond—so they can lead fulfilling lives and build a more just world. KIPP is a national network of tuition-free, public charter schools open to all students. There are 255 college-preparatory KIPP schools in 20 states and the District of Columbia, serving more than 100,000 students. Nationally, KIPP students are graduating four-year colleges at three times the national average for low-income students. Who we are: KIPP Colorado Public Schools is a network of six free college-preparatory public charter schools open to all students. Our 350-person staff educates 2,600 students from ECE to 12th grade. At KIPP Colorado, we partner with our KIPPsters, educators, families and communities to ensure that we are all united around the goal of a choice-filled future for our KIPPsters. Our KIPP Forward Team supports our 1,000+ high school Alumni as they create their own paths. Our core values of excellence, belonging, belief, advocacy and courage are central to who we are and how we operate at all levels of our organization. What we do: We believe in the unique gifts and brilliance of every student. We believe in setting a high bar for joy and academic excellence to ensure the infinite possibilities our students have before them become a reality. jobs.description: Employer: JFCS of Greater Philadelphia Expires: 10/15/2026 Position SummaryThe Operations and Inventory Coordinator plays a critical role in the successful operation of the Our Closet program by overseeing warehouse activities, inventory management, donation processing, volunteer coordination, and logistical support for clothing distribution initiatives. This position is responsible for ensuring donated clothing and related items are received, sorted, organized, stored, tracked, and distributed efficiently to support Our Closet pop-up shops, crisis clothing requests, reentry initiatives, small closets, and other program services.In this role, the coordinator maintains a safe, organized, and efficient warehouse environment, coordinates inventory preparation for community distribution events, supports volunteer engagement activities, and ensures program resources are readily available to meet client needs. This position works closely with the Community Relations Coordinator and Events & Logistics Coordinator to ensure seamless coordination across program operations, inventory, community sites and distribution events. The Operations & Inventory Coordinator works closely with the Community Relations Coordinator and Events & Logistics Coordinator to ensure seamless coordination across program operations, inventory, community sites, and distribution events. This position serves as a representative of JFCS and Our Closet, fostering positive relationships with donors, volunteers, community partners, and staff while advancing the mission of providing dignified access to clothing and essential resources for vulnerable members of the community.Essential Duties and ResponsibilitiesWarehouse Operations and Inventory ManagementOversee daily warehouse distributing donated clothing and related items.Maintain accurate inventory systems and processes to support program operations and reporting needs.Monitor inventory trends and anticipate program needs to support adequate clothing and supply levels for upcoming pop-ups, Small Closets, crisis requests, reentry services, and other program activities.Ensure donated items meet quality standards and are properly processed for distribution.Organize warehouse space to maximize efficiency, accessibility, and safety.Coordinate the preparation and packing of inventory for pop-up shops, crisis clothing requests, reentry packages, small closets, and other program initiatives.Conduct periodic inventory counts and assist with inventory audits and reconciliation activities.Maintain supplies, equipment, storage areas, and warehouse resources necessary for program operations.Receive, inspect, sort, and process incoming donations from individuals, businesses, schools, faith communities, and partner organizations.Coordinate donation drop-offs and pickups as assigned.Ensure timely processing and distribution of donated goods.Assist with loading, unloading, transporting, and organizing donations, supplies, and equipment.Coordinate logistics related to inventory transportation between the warehouse, pop-up locations, offices, and community partner sites.Develop and manage delivery routes for crisis clothing packages, coordinating delivery schedules and logistics to ensure packages are delivered efficiently and in a timely manner.Maintain records related to donations, inventory movement, and distribution activities.Recruit, schedule, supervise, and support volunteers participating in warehouse operations and sorting projects.Provide volunteer orientation, training, and ongoing guidance related to warehouse processes and safety procedures.Lead volunteer sorting events and service projects.Assign volunteer tasks and monitor productivity and workflow.Foster a positive volunteer experience through effective communication, engagement, and recognition.Ensure volunteers adhere to warehouse safety standards and program procedures.Prepare crisis clothing packages, reentry clothing packages, and other client-focused distributions in accordance with program guidelines.Coordinate with the Community Relations Coordinator to monitor and fulfill inventory needs for Small Closets, including preparing and transporting restocking inventory as needed.Coordinate the preparation of inventory and supplies needed for pop-up shops, small closets, and community distribution events.Support program staff in meeting urgent clothing requests and special client needs.Assist with maintaining quality standards for all items distributed through program documentation, and administrative tasks within established timelines.Maintain confidentiality of client, donor, volunteer, and agency information.Participate in Our Closet, JFCS, and community events as assigned.Adhere to all agency policies, procedures, safety requirements, and applicable regulations.Participate in warehouse safety training and operational meetings.Perform other duties and special projects as assigned.Knowledge of inventory management principles and warehouse operations.Ability to organize and maintain efficient inventory systems.Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality control.Ability to coordinate multiple logistical priorities simultaneously.Exceptional organizational and time-management skills.Ability to prioritize tasks and manage workflow efficiently.Demonstrates dependability, accountability, and sound judgment.Maintains accurate records and documentation.Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills.Ability to work effectively with volunteers, donors, community partners, and colleagues.Demonstrates professionalism and customer service excellence in all interactions.Ability to provide clear direction and guidance to volunteers and support staff.Ability to work independently and collaboratively.Demonstrates initiative and effective problem-solving skills.Flexibility to respond to changing program and operational needs.Ability to identify efficiencies and recommend process improvements.Commitment to maintaining a safe, clean, and organized work environment.Ability to follow and enforce warehouse safety procedures and agency policies.Maintains confidentiality and professionalism in all aspects of work.Proficiency with Microsoft Office 365 applications including Outlook, Word, Excel, Teams, and SharePoint.Ability to learn and utilize inventory tracking systems, agency databases, and reporting platforms.Experience using spreadsheets and inventory management tools preferred.High school diploma or GED required.Associate degree or coursework in logistics, business, inventory management, nonprofit management, operations, or a related field preferred.Minimum of two (2) years of successful work jobs.title: Peer Support Specialist - Men's Center (Overnight) at City Union Mission
jobs.description: Employer: City Union Mission Expires: 10/15/2026 Who We Are:For over 100 years, City Union Mission has offered hope to men, women and children experiencing huge challenges. Homelessness. Addiction. Poverty. We start by extending a welcoming hand and helping to meet their immediate needs - food, shelter, clothing. From there, we offer them a new foundation for their lives through Christ - and life-changing programs that move them toward physical, emotional and spiritual wholeness. Job Summary:Our emergency shelter mission at our Men's Center and Women & Family Center is to serve as a strategic safety net for the city by providing immediate, short-term, and dignified refuge for individuals and families in crisis: protecting life, meeting basic needs, sharing the Gospel at each point of care, and creating a clear bridge to appropriate next steps.The Peer Support Specialist is responsible for the overall environment of the center and the well-being of every client in the building, ensuring access to essential supports such as shelter, meals, hygiene, and supervision while prioritizing safety and stabilization. This role reinforces that emergency shelter is a life-safety, short-term service; focused on keeping people safe tonight while serving as a bridge to appropriate next steps.
